panels.general_description: Grayscale coronal MRI of the abdomen and pelvis with one white arrow near the right kidney.
panels.detailed_description: Single grayscale coronal-plane MRI of the lower torso. The image is wider at the top, with a curved black border at the top and bottom, and a small letter H is printed at the top center. A column of vertebral bodies with dark discs runs down the center. On the left side of the picture is a large homogeneous dark gray region with a round-oval structure of mixed bright and gray signal at its lower inner edge, containing a bright central region branching toward the midline; a short white arrow in the lower left of this structure points up and to the right toward a thin dark channel beside the bright central region. On the right side of the picture are gray loop-like structures with rounded dark segments and a small bright ring. Hip bones and pelvic soft tissue fill the lower third, with dark round structures near the bottom center. Bright subcutaneous fat lines both flanks, and a short white horizontal scale bar sits at the lower right with no printed number. No other text, patient label, date or panel letter is visible.

panels.detailed_description: Single grayscale axial MRI of the pelvis. A large bright rounded-rectangular structure with a thin dark wall lies at the top center. Behind it, a mixed gray region of soft tissue and a dark round-oval structure with a thicker wall lie in the central pelvis. A short white arrow just behind the lower left of the bright structure points up and to the right toward the interface between the bright structure and the tissue behind it. Two round structures with dark rims and a gray center lie one on each side of the pelvis, at the left and right. Bright subcutaneous fat surrounds the pelvis, with dark muscle bands at the lower sides, and thin vessels and small dark spots lie under the skin at the top. A white horizontal scale bar sits at the lower right with no printed number. No text, panel letter, patient label or date is visible.
